I cannot reliably state the exact SCOP 1.75 versus newer SCOPe domain definitions for PDB 1acc chain A from pretrained knowledge alone. I did not read any file or use the network, so I cannot check the release files. Verify the before and after segments in the SCOP 1.75 and SCOPe release domain-boundary files before relying on any specific claim, including the 1acc chain A identity and its domain count.

What the kind of change usually means: when a chain's domain segmentation is revised between releases, the usual cause is curator re-judgment of compact structural units (splitting or merging segments, or moving a boundary). It is not normally a change in evolutionary history. Domains are structural segments and are the closest unit to evolutionary modules. Their boundaries are curated and can be discontinuous in sequence, so a boundary shift does not by itself show that the underlying family, superfamily, or fold changed. Evolutionary strength must be judged at the level of the matched segment: a family or superfamily call should only be trusted if the segment-level alignment supports it. Class and fold calls are coarser and should be more stable across such a revision than exact domain boundaries.

How this should affect homology searches: (1) Do not transfer SCOP 1.75 domain IDs, boundaries, or superfamily labels to SCOPe releases by name; remap by residue ranges and check the release version. (2) Profile, HMM, or domain-library searches built on old boundaries may give partial coverage of a new segment or cover two new segments at once, so use coverage-aware scoring and re-run or re-index against the current release. (3) A boundary difference alone is not evidence of a different fold or of non-homology. (4) Treat any single-hit annotation for 1acc chain A as provisional until the release-specific mapping is checked.
